archetype.name: Bubble Team (goalie-propped)
archetype.definition: A team whose possession and chance numbers sit in the bottom third of the league, but elite goaltending from its starter and a strong top pair of skaters have put a playoff-pace record on the board.

report.headline: Ullmark's saves have Ottawa at 5-2 while the shot share points lower
report.take:
Ottawa is 5-2-0 and tied with Boston atop the Atlantic, but the site has it 15th of 32, and that gap is the story. At 5-on-5 the Senators are getting outplayed: a 46.5 xGF % (24th) and a 44 CF % (27th) mean opponents have the puck and the better looks most nights. The record is real points in the bank. It is not yet evidence of a good team.

What bridges the gap is Linus Ullmark. Through five starts he is at a .948 Save % and 6.9 GSAx, sixth on the goalie tab. Samuel Ersson has gone the other way at .829 and -4.2. Up front, Tim Stützle has 11 points and plays like a top-ten center, and Thomas Chabot logs 27-plus minutes a night at a +7. Behind those two the drop-off is steep. Dylan Cozens has 14 shots and no goals with a .397 xGF %, Tyler Kleven sits at .297, and Carter Yakemchuk is a -4. The wins came narrowly: one-goal games against Toronto, Philadelphia and Nashville, plus two 4-1 wins. The two losses were blowouts, 3-5 at Detroit and 2-7 at home to St. Louis. That adds up to a +2 differential and a Pts vs Goal Diff of 1.6, third in the league, along with a 101.9 PDO.

History makes this an odd flip. Last season Ottawa drove play, with a .556 xGF % and the 8th-ranked offense, and lost ground because its goalies were -24 GSAx. This year the goaltending has been fixed for now and the territorial game has disappeared. Seven games is too few to say the possession collapse is permanent, especially for a roster that controlled play a year ago. It is enough to say the 5-2 mark is borrowing from Ullmark and from close-game breaks.

The Senators look like a bubble team that will win when Ullmark is excellent, and that only works if the 5-on-5 game drifts back toward last year's form. The special teams are a separate drag. A 15.2% power play (24th) and a 78.6% penalty kill (21st) are giving nothing back, so 5-on-5 has to carry them.

strengths.title: Ullmark is stealing games
strengths.body: Ullmark's .948 and 6.9 GSAx are the main reason a team being out-chanced has a winning record, and they mask Ersson's rough start in the team total. He has a track record of strong seasons in Ottawa's history (the 2024-25 team was +23.7 GSAx), so he should stay an asset. A sub-1.30 GAA is not a pace anyone keeps, though.

strengths.title: Stützle and Chabot drive the top
strengths.body: Stützle has 11 points and a positive xGF % in nearly 22 minutes a night, ninth among centers on the site. Chabot plays more than 27 minutes, sits seventh among defensemen, and is +7 with a .551 xGF %. Both are on the right side of the chance battle while the team as a whole is not. Stützle's 5 goals on 13 shots will cool, but the underlying play looks real.

concerns.title: Getting out-possessed at 5-on-5
concerns.body: A 46.5 xGF % and 44 CF % put Ottawa in the bottom third on both measures of who controls play. That is a sharp reversal from last season's .556 xGF %, and the roster has shown it can do better. Small samples can still swing it back. Left alone, this is what turns a 5-2 start into a .500 team once the saves normalize.

concerns.title: Record outrunning the margin
concerns.body: Ten standings points on a +2 differential is exactly what the third-best Pts vs Goal Diff in the league looks like. The wins came close, and the losses were lopsided. With a 101.9 PDO on top of that, some of the record should give back.

concerns.title: Wingers and the third pair leak
concerns.body: Opposing wingers are scoring well above their own averages against Ottawa, 25th in the league, and wingers account for a far larger share of points against than the league norm. Kleven's .297 and Yakemchuk's .373 xGF % in heavy minutes point to the second and third pairings as part of the cause. Special teams aren't covering for it, with both the PP and PK in the 20s.

trend.note: Wins have come in tight games, with a three-game streak and no back-to-back losses. Both losses were blowouts, the latest a 2-7 home loss to St. Louis, which fits a team leaning on its goalie night to night.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games and two weak opponents in a four-game week
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against the Islanders. They are 3-3-0 with a +0.67 goal differential per game built almost entirely on an A-graded goaltending group (5.6 GSAx, 4th) and a 104.3 PDO, and they hold opposing forwards furthest under expectation of almost anyone. Expect a low-event game that hinges on whether Ottawa's goalie can match theirs. Then comes a trip to winless Philadelphia, last on the site, last in xGF % and last in offense. Ottawa only beat the Flyers 2-1 at home the first time, so even this one isn't free.

The back half is at home. Florida is the real test: a 55 CF % (5th) and B+ forwards, exactly the kind of possession team that exposes Ottawa's shot-share problem. San Jose follows on the second night of a back-to-back. The Sharks are 27th in goals against and have the worst record in the league at holding opposing wingers to their averages, which suits Batherson, Giroux and Amadio. Three home games plus the two weakest opponents make this a chance to bank points. The Islanders and Panthers will show whether the 5-on-5 game is fixable.

keyMatchups.title: Florida's possession vs Ottawa's
keyMatchups.body: Florida's 55 CF % against Ottawa's 44 is the widest territorial gap Ottawa faces this week. If the Senators spend the night defending again, the game falls on the goalie. This matchup is the clearest read on whether the shot-share problem is structural.

keyMatchups.title: Islanders' goaltending wall
keyMatchups.body: New York's goalies are 4th in GSAx and their skaters hold opposing forwards well under expectation. Ottawa's 19th-ranked offense and 24th-ranked power play will have to manufacture goals. A low-scoring game is likely.

keyMatchups.title: Ottawa wingers against San Jose
keyMatchups.body: The Sharks let wingers outscore their averages by nearly a point a game, 27th in the league, and their goaltending grades D-. Batherson has the best xGF % among Ottawa's forwards at .594 and is the obvious beneficiary.

weekAhead.watch: Who starts the back-to-back against Florida and San Jose, and whether Ersson can post a respectable game, because the record has rested on Ullmark.

restOfSeason.body:
Ullmark should stay good, though not .948 good, and the close-game luck behind a Pts vs Goal Diff of 1.6 tends to even out. That puts pressure on the 5-on-5 numbers to recover. The case for optimism is last season, when a similar core posted a .556 xGF % and an 8th-ranked offense. A drift back toward even possession is more likely than staying 27th in CF %. If that happens with competent goaltending, this is a playoff-caliber team for the first time in a while. If the shot share stays in the mid-40s, Ottawa becomes a bubble team that lives and dies with Ullmark.

Special teams are the other lever. Ottawa ran a power play in the 23-24% range the last two seasons, so the 15.2% start looks more like noise than identity. The penalty kill has been below average for years, so don't expect much help there.
swingFactors: Whether the 5-on-5 shot share returns toward last season's level
Ullmark's health and workload, and whether Ersson stabilizes

confidence.note: Seven games; possession and save percentages are far from stable.
